negative_findings.description: No dedicated Serbian-language job/recruitment board for Serb-majority Kosovo surfaced. Searches for bank hiring in Gračanica returned Bosnian Gračanica (MF Banka, radiogracanica.ba, gracanica.gov.ba) — a systematic homonym trap.
negative_findings.result_summary: Hiring signal for this cell appears to travel through general news items about 'konkursi' at Serbia-funded institutions rather than through a job portal.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A5 jobs/hiring coverage for the sr dimension will have to be reconstructed from news text and employer sites; any collector must hard-filter Bosnian Gračanica by domain (.ba) and by co-occurring terms.

negative_findings.description: Searches for named appointments (imenovan direktor) at banks operating in or serving Serb-majority Kosovo returned no sr-language appointment items; results collapsed onto generic CBK/BQK governance pages in English.

negative_findings.why_it_matters: Leadership-move intelligence here likely has to come from bank corporate sites, NBS registers and business registries rather than sr media.

coverage_gaps.description: Bank-side primary sources for this cell are thin: no branch-locator dataset, careers page, or annual report was actually opened for Poštanska štedionica or NLB Komercijalna banka in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Resolve and register the two banks' corporate sites; set up periodic diffing of their branch/expozitura locators, which is the cleanest machine-readable organization-change signal available for the dinar dimension.

coverage_gaps.description: No Kosovo-side registry check was made for whether Serbian-licensed banks or their staff-serving entities appear in Kosovo's business registry (ARBK) or CBK licensed-institution list under sr-transliterated names.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Cross-check ARBK and CBK/BQK licensed-institution lists for Serbian-name entities and transliterations (Poštanska/Postanska/Poshtanska), which would convert media claims into registry-grade evidence.

coverage_gaps.description: Most retrieved evidence clusters around the 2024 dinar ban and branch closures; little 2025-2026 material surfaced despite the current date being August 2026.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Re-run this cell's queries with explicit 2025/2026 date constraints and directly on KoSSev/Kosovo Online site search, to establish whether coverage genuinely thinned or search recency bias suppressed it.

coverage_gaps.description: All queries were run in Latin-script Serbian; Cyrillic-script variants (Поштанска штедионица, филијала, запослени, именован директор) were not attempted, and Politika/RTS/kim.gov.rs publish substantially in Cyrillic.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Duplicate the query set in Cyrillic and add script-normalisation (Latin<->Cyrillic transliteration) to the collector's matching layer.

coverage_gaps.description: Several enclave outlets (notably RTV KIM) appear to distribute primarily via Facebook, which is not collectable under normal scraping constraints.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Decide a policy for social-first local outlets — permitted API access, manual review cadence, or explicit exclusion documented as a known blind spot.

brief: The Serbian-language layer of Kosovo banking intelligence is small, concentrated, and largely news-driven: KoSSev is the anchor source for North Kosovo, supplemented by Kosovo Online, Danas, Vreme, RFE/RL's Serbian service and a handful of hyperlocal broadcasters (Kontakt Plus, RTV KIM, Gračanica Online), with Politika/RTS/RT Balkan usable only as framed, state-aligned primary-statement archives. The recurring intelligence in this cell is organization change rather than hiring: closures and seizures of Poštanska štedionica and NLB Komercijalna banka units, mobile expozitura at administrative crossings, detained bank staff, and the euro-only CBK regulation that reroutes how Serbia-funded employees in Kosovo are paid. Structural, machine-readable evidence is currently missing — no bank branch locator, careers page, or registry entry was actually opened this pass — so the highest-value next step is resolving the two banks' corporate domains and cross-checking ARBK/CBK registries. Two systematic risks should be encoded in any collector: the Bosnian-Gračanica homonym trap that poisons sr hiring searches, and the absence of Cyrillic-script queries, which likely suppressed Politika, RTS and kim.gov.rs material.
